speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, before tlie House adjourns I beg, by com- ' mand of His Excellency, to lay on tbe table of tbe House certain papers respecting tbe removal from office of tbe Earl of Dun-donald, and I beg at tbe same time to move that the papers, be printed and that rule 94 be suspended. '

Before tbe motion is put, I would like to inquire whether or not the papers include all letters written by the Minister of Agriculture to the Department of Militia, as well as to the proposed officers in the regiment-with respect to their political opinions, for example ; because if we are to have a record of the correspondence, the result of the interference of the Minister of Agriculture in this matter, we ought to have a complete record, and not any partial statement, such as that which was presented to the House the other day, and which was contradicted by the Minister of Agriculture himself when he came to speak on the subject. Therefore, I would ask my right lion, friend whether we are to have- everything, or only such documents as it suits the purpose of the government to produce V

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
speechtext: I may say to my hon. friend that it suits the purpose of the government to produce everything. My hon. friend has no right to assume anything else. I may say that the papers which I produce to-day are not complete, but we propose to bring some others to-morrow.

Am I to understand
then, that it is the intention of the government to produce, without evasion and without equivocation, all letters which have been written by the Minister of Agriculture with respect to this matter, whether to persons connected with the Department of Militia or to persons proposed as officers in this regiment, in order that the House may judge of the character of the interference which undoubtedly he did make in the affairs of this regiment. That is what I would like to know, and I think I have a right to ask my right hon. friend, because without that the record will not be complete.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
speechtext: I havg to say to my hon. friend that it is the purpose of the government in this instance, as in all instances, to bring down, without evasion or equivocation, all papers which are on record and on file connected with this matter.

But, I want my right hon. friend to understand that I am not satisfied with all papers that are on file in the Department of Militia. The letters of the Minister of Agriculture to which I refer,

and of which evidence can be produced if necessary, are not on file in the Department of Militia ; but, nevertheless, they have been written and do constitute an interference by the Minister of Agriculture in the affairs of this regiment. All* I am asking and want to know is whether it is the intention of the government tP produce these as well as the documents on file in the Department of Militia V Because I venture respectfully to submit to my right hon. friend that without those documents the record which the country will desire to receive will not be complete.
iSir WILFRID LAURIER. I can add nothing to what I have said already, and I am sure the Minister of Agriculture is as anxious to produce everything as I am, because he has nothing to hide in reference to this matter.
All I have to say is that if the government will not produce all of those letters, I will endeavour to supplement the return myself.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
speechtext: Then I understand there has been some interference with the Department of Militia on the part of my hon. friend.

My right hon. friend has no reason to suggest anything of the kind, because I have told him-and he understands it, if he understands the English
language at all-

He understands that the letters to which I refer are not on file in the Department of Militia, but their existence has been public property in certain communities in this country for many days past. The Minister of Agriculture knows of them and has copies of them I have no doubt. They are not documents which are on file, but they constitute an interference by him, and I would think it only fair, if the government propose to make a complete, fair and truthful record of this matter, that these documents should be produced as well as those which are on file. That is all I venture to suggest, and I trust that my right hon. friend will not regard me as unreasonable in making that moderate request respectfully and sincerely so that the House and the country may have an opportunity of judging fairly in this matter.
